questions.q: What did David and Alan do while they waited in a hollow for the morning mist to rise?
choices: Made a dish of drammach and held a council of war
Built a small fire of heather and dried their clothes
Cut branches of fir to make a shelter for the day
Slept in turns while the other watched the hill tops
questions.evidence: made ourselves a dish of drammach, and held a council of war

questions.q: Alan says, "this is the kittle bit." What does "kittle" mean here?
choices: Tricky and dangerous
Short and easy
Wet and muddy
Already finished
questions.evidence: this is the kittle bit

questions.q: Which way did Alan decide they should go?
choices: East, across the open moors
South, through the Campbell country
North, toward the far coast
West, back into the hills of Appin
questions.evidence: we'll can strike east

questions.q: When David said "East be it!" quite cheerily, what was he secretly thinking?
choices: That they would both be better off going separate ways
That Alan had picked the most dangerous road on purpose
That they ought to wait in the hollow until dark after all
That he would rather go back and give himself up to the soldiers
questions.evidence: let me take any other, it would be the best for both of us

questions.q: Why did Alan say the flat moor was a bad place to cross by daylight?
choices: Soldiers coming over a hill could spy them miles away
The bogs and peaty pools were too deep to wade
Wild deer on the moor would give away their position
There was no water anywhere on it for them to drink all day
questions.evidence: they can spy you miles away

questions.q: Since they had no clock, how was David to know when to wake Alan from his watch?
choices: By the shadow of a sprig of heath stuck in the ground
By counting the cries of the moorfowl and the pewees
By watching the herd of deer cross to the east
By waiting until the water in the brandy bottle was gone
questions.evidence: Alan stuck a sprig of heath in the ground to serve instead

questions.q: What happened while David was keeping the second watch?
choices: He dozed off, and horse-soldiers came near from the south-east
He saw a herd of deer and woke Alan to hunt them
Cluny's sentries crept up and took away all of their weapons and food
A grouse flew up and he woke Alan by mistake too early
questions.evidence: a body of horse-soldiers had come down during my sleep

questions.q: How did Alan react when he saw David had slept through his watch?
choices: He gave one quick ugly, anxious look, and that was all
He shouted at David and called him a coward and a Whig
He laughed and told David it did not matter at all
He said he would never trust David with a watch again
questions.evidence: which was all the reproach I had of him

questions.q: Which mountain did Alan decide they must reach before morning?
choices: Ben Alder
Ben Nevis
Ben Lomond
Ben More
questions.evidence: Its name is Ben Alder

questions.q: How did Alan and David move across the moor to get away from the soldiers?
choices: Running on their hands and knees in the low places
Riding two horses that they took from the dragoons
Wading along the bed of a shallow stream
Walking upright behind a line of dead fir trees
questions.evidence: run forward on his hands and knees

questions.q: What sometimes made them lie as still as the dead, afraid to breathe?
choices: A grouse rising out of the heather with a clap of wings
A trumpet blowing from the far side of the moor
A dragoon riding straight toward their heather bush
A hunting dog barking somewhere close behind them in the heather
questions.evidence: when a grouse rose out of the heather with a clap of wings

questions.q: What kept David going when the pain was so bad he would gladly have given up?
choices: His fear of Alan
His hope of reaching Queensferry
His anger at the soldiers
His wish to see Cluny
questions.evidence: Nothing but the fear of Alan lent me enough of a false kind of courage

questions.q: What does David's description of Alan's red-and-white face and whistling breath show?
choices: Alan was suffering as badly as David but would not give in
Alan had been wounded by a shot from one of the dragoons
Alan was sick with a fever he had caught in the bogs
Alan was angry with David and could hardly bring himself to speak to him
questions.evidence: I was driven to marvel at the man's endurance

questions.q: What did the soldiers do at the first gloaming of the night?
choices: Gathered at a trumpet call and camped by a fire
Turned north and rode toward Ben Alder
Split into small groups to search the bogs and hags
Rode back south toward the Campbell country
questions.evidence: they had built a fire and camped for the night

questions.q: When David said he had no strength left, what did Alan offer, and how did David respond?
choices: Alan offered to carry him, and David was shamed into following
Alan offered to stop for an hour, and David fell asleep at once
Alan offered him the last of the brandy, and David drank it all
Alan offered to leave him hidden, and David begged him to stay
questions.evidence: the sight of so much resolution shamed me

questions.q: During the long night march, how did David feel toward Alan?
choices: He hated him as the cause of all his pain
He loved him like a brother for his courage
He pitied him for carrying the heavy great-coat
He trusted him more than ever before
questions.evidence: of Alan, who was the cause of it, with hatred

questions.q: What happened as Alan and David went down a heathery brae at dawn?
choices: Ragged men leaped out and held dirks at their throats
They fell into a peaty pool and lost their weapons
They saw the dragoons riding up the other side of the glen
They found a shepherd's hut and slept inside it
questions.evidence: three or four ragged men leaped out

questions.q: Who turned out to be the men who ambushed them?
choices: Out-sentries belonging to Cluny Macpherson
Campbell men hunting for the murderer of the Red Fox
Robbers who lived wild in the hills of Ben Alder
Red-coat soldiers dressed in Highland clothes
questions.evidence: They are Cluny's men

questions.q: Why was David so surprised to hear that Cluny was still in the country?
choices: He had thought that Cluny had long ago fled to France
He had heard that Cluny had been hanged by the king
He believed Cluny had joined the side of the Campbells
He had been told Cluny was too old to lead his clan
questions.evidence: I had supposed him long ago in France

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A painful escape across the moor that ends with Cluny's men taking them in
A battle between Alan and the dragoons in the middle of the moor
David and Alan splitting up so that each of them can go his own way home safely
A long rest in a hidden cave while the soldiers search Appin
questions.evidence: We got through in the nick of time
